Status Effects

From Limbus Company Wiki
Jump to navigation Jump to search
Status Effects
Enemy-Exclusive Status Effects

Status Effects are conditions that can be applied to units on either side of a battle through the use of Passives, Skills, E.G.O Gifts and even other status effects.

Overview

A status effect can use up to two values to function, which will be called 'modes' here for clarity:

  • Zero-value mode, where the value is always fixed at 1 and has no inherent effect on the status effect's strength.
  • Single-value mode, where the value is typically called Count, Stack or simply Value.
  • Double-value mode, where one value is called Potency and the other Count. Generally, Potency determines the strength of the effect, while Count determines its duration.

In single-value or double-value modes, if one or more of the values reach 0, the status effect is removed from the unit. Additionally, the values of a status effect are always consumed before they are gained or inflicted.

If the status effect uses both values, the Potency will be displayed on the bottom left, with the Count on the bottom right. Otherwise, the value is always displayed on the bottom left.

Status effects also come with a few attributes:

  • Base Value, the initial value of the status effect upon infliction if no value is specified.
  • Max Value, the maximum value of the status effect. The default Max Value is 99.

Status effects are also separated into three categories:

  • Positive status effects, which are highlighted in yellow.
  • Neutral status effects, which are highlighted in brown.
  • Negative status effects, which are highlighted in red.

Note that a status being classified as positive or negative does not necessarily mean its effects are fully beneficial or detrimental. From the gameplay perspective, this classification primarily matters for the purposes of effects such as "Deal +10% damage for every negative status effect on this unit".

Keyword Status Effects

Keyword Status Effects
Burn - Bleed - Tremor - Rupture - Sinking - Poise - Charge

Buffs

Positive Status Effects (or Buffs) provide beneficial effects to the receiver.

Neutral Effects

Neutral Status Effects either have both positive and negative effects, or have no significant effect on the user.
Some Neutral Status Effects are used as expendable resources, with Skills being enhanced or cancelled due to the Value of these Effects.

Name Description Source (If Exclusive)
Clashable Guard - On Clash Win: raise the target's Stagger Threshold by this unit's final Clash Power.

Trivia

  • Limbus Company uses two different sets of descriptions for status effects: one for when it is viewed in the descriptions of Skills and Passives, and one for when it is inflicted onto and listed under a unit.
    • While most status effects only possess minor discrepancies between these two, some can have significant differences, such as Weak-resist DMG Boost, which lists the damage increase as "10% per Count" on the first and "1% per Count" on the latter. The status effect itself functions based on the "1% per Count" basis.
      • This discrepancy likely caused confusion among the developers of the game as well, as the Peccatulum Irae Class 2 only gained 1 Weak-resist DMG Boost from its Skills, likely due to the assumption that this would result in a 10% damage increase when it is only 1% in reality. This was likely caused by the fact that Weak-resist DMG Boost did not appear as part of any Skill or Passive description, thus never requiring the first set.

"Burn, burn, burn—y'see, Kid, fire's not the be-all, end-all solution to every problem you've got. When it comes to using heat-modulating weapons like these, the deciding factors often come down to when to spark the flame, and how hot you let it burn.
"Yeah, that's why I'm always chewing your ear off about how important it is to feel the 'moment' that comes with the territory of using heat-modulating weapons. But on the other hand… when that 'moment' tells you to burn it all down, don't hold back and just let it rip. … Hm? Oh, you want to know who's the best in the field?"
"Hmm, let's see… Well, the best of the best's got to be the Vermilion Cross, I'd wager."

The Dawn Office of this Mirror World, unlike that of others, has yet to completely lose its fervor. One can reasonably conjecture that the two leading Fixers of this Office have sufficient competence to find work as Grade 1 of the vocation.

However, it must be stated that the Office and its Fixers' grades do not vary from those of other observed Mirror Worlds, as combat capability is hardly the sole criterion by which the Grades are assigned. Failure to meet the conditions stipulated by the contract clauses to the client's satisfaction, eschewal of high-risk contracts that contribute to the advancement of Fixer Grades—these are all conditions that limit one's mobility along the ladder of Fixer Grades.

"Granted, battle instinct, in most cases, can only be properly demonstrated in the heat of battle. One might refer to this process as a "warm up," although that term is perhaps too simple. In any case, a heightened natural battle instinct will help you offset the gear's structural and technical vulnerabilities. This is how you may raise the baseline of your performance threshold. Assist Attack- If unit A applies this effect to unit B: Unit B follows up with an Unopposed Attack with its Skill 1 against the same enemy unit A attacked with its Skill. Activates at unit A's Attack End.
- The Skill used as an Assist Attack does not affect Unit B's upcoming Skills list.
Target SpottedIf unit A applies this effect to unit B: Unit B follows up with an Unopposed Attack with its Skill 2 against the same enemy Unit A attacked with its Skill. Activates at Unit A's Attack End.
- The Skill used due to this effect does not affect Unit B's upcoming Skills list.
Exalted Command- If unit A applies this effect to unit B: Unit B follows up with an Unopposed Attack with its Base Skill 3 against the same enemy unit A attacked with its Skill. Activates at unit A's Attack End. (Does not activate as Empowered Skills)
- The Skill used as an Assist Attack does not affect Unit B's upcoming Skills list.
- Does not activate if affected ally's Skill 3 is not unlocked.
Your Will Guides My Blade.- If unit A applies this effect to unit B: Unit B follows up with an Unopposed Attack with its Skill 1 against the same enemy unit A attacked with its Skill. Activates at unit A's Skill Attack End.
- The Skill used as an Assist Attack does not affect Unit B's upcoming Skills list.
Melee Support- If unit A applies this effect to unit B: Unit B follows up with an Unopposed Attack with the 'Melee Support' Skill against the same enemy that attacked Unit A. Activates at Unit A's Skill End.
- The Skill used due to the 'Melee Support' effect does not affect Unit B's upcoming Skills list.
